title: Anxious Moment As Water Falls — Savoy water tower topples
text:
Anxious Moment
As Water Falls

3-10-57[?]

SAVOY — A tiny tidal wave hit two Savoy families at dusk Thursday when a 50,000 gallon city water tower toppled. One of the steel legs supporting the tower got a bend in it Sunday when 60-mph winds raked the town, and the weakened support finally collapsed sending tons of water cascading down on the two nearby trailer home residences.

For Raymond Langford it was just another in a series of calamities that have befallen him. A little more than a year ago the service station he owns in Savoy burned to the ground. He had only partial insurance.

Three months ago his house burned and again it was only partially covered by insurance. He bought the trailer house and had it moved behind his rebuilt service station, which sits on the south side of U.S. 82 in the shadow of the water tower.

When the tower toppled, it washed his trailer 10 feet off its concrete block foundation, snapping water, sewer and power lines, ripping down his television antenna and just pulling the bottom out of the trailer. The interior of the trailer house was a shambles.

C. C. Waldrum, who lived just east of the toppled tower, got the brunt of the water.

"It sounded like a bomb explosion," said Waldrum. "The wall of water that gushed out of the huge tank hit my trailer house at window level. It smashed my pickup truck against the chain link fence that surrounded my property.

"One storage house where we kept most of our food and other materials was flattened. My brick walk around the yard was washed out. An air conditioner under the trailer was destroyed and a work shed has more than a foot of silt in it," Waldrum said.

Waldrum admitted he had been uneasy about the tower since the Sunday storm. "We had hail, sleet, rain and wind Sunday, and that old tower almost went then," he declared.

Claud Strickland, Savoy city secretary, said the tank was installed in 1952 and used primarily for storage. He said the city carried a $20,000 insurance policy against wind damage or fire on the tank.

"We put up a 100,000-gallon tank last year and coupled with another 33,000 gallon overhead storage tank, used the 50,000 gallon tower just as an emergency supply," Strickland said.

Strickland said the council meets a week from Tuesday. He said by then insurance adjusters will have had a chance to view the damage and the council will be in a position to know where they stand.

The collapsing tower shook houses all over town and quickly attracted a big crowd of spectators. Strickland said there was no interruption in the town's water service.
notes: Date handwritten '3-10-57' in image margin, but given context (50,000-gallon tank installed 1952, 100,000-gallon tank 'put up last year') the actual year is likely 1967 or nearby; the '57' may be a page number or partial annotation. U.S. 82 runs through Savoy. The 50,000-gallon tower had been demoted to emergency supply after newer tanks were installed. No publication name visible.
